residents.bio: Warehouse lead @ Kinzie. Mattoon raised, Des Plaines now. Car guy. Its 'you're' not 'your.'
residents.backstory: Jesse grew up in Mattoon, the kid brother who took apart the lawnmower and couldn't put it back together. His sister Amanda left for the suburbs first and he followed at twenty-two, landing at Kinzie Freight by O'Hare, where he runs a shift crew well and his own finances badly. He has owned seven cars in seven years, every one a 'steal' he found online, overpaid for in cash, babied for two weeks and then ignored until it died; the crew at Kinzie keeps a running tally on the breakroom whiteboard. The newest is a red 2004 Mustang convertible with a soft top that leaks, and he is in love. He picks up hobbies as fast as cars — fishing, a smoker, a guitar he never tuned — and drops them as fast. He is loud, funny and generous with his time, corrects everyone's grammar while mangling his own, and makes cracks about Indian call centers and gas station owners that he thinks are just jokes.

residents.bio: Inventory analyst. Mount Prospect. I count things. Reselling Bulls jerseys, inquire within.
residents.backstory: Jake grew up in Mount Prospect two streets from where he rents a basement apartment now, the youngest of three Polish-American brothers who communicated mostly by roasting each other. He studied supply chain at NIU, got hired at Kinzie Freight as an inventory analyst and is quietly excellent at it: his counts are right, his spreadsheets are clean, and he enjoys being right more than being liked. Online he is the guy in the comments. He needles people for sport, especially Jesse Hensley, whose car purchases he has turned into a recurring series, and he picks fights with anyone who brags about money or posts a cop story. Occasionally he is genuinely, devastatingly funny, which is why people keep him around. He runs a side hustle reselling vintage Bulls jerseys and sneakers out of his parents' garage and promotes it in the middle of arguments. He likes Donna Novotny's food posts more than he admits.

residents.bio: Ops manager, Kinzie Freight. Husband, dad of two, owner of one ridiculous dog. Norridge.
residents.backstory: Marko came to Chicago from Kragujevac at sixteen, finished high school at Steinmetz speaking half English and half Serbian, and worked his way up from forklift driver to operations manager at Kinzie Freight in twenty-five years. He runs the building the way he runs everything: calmly, with a joke, and with the opposite opinion of whoever spoke last, just to make them think. He married Jelena, a pharmacist he met at a Serbian church picnic, and they live in Norridge with their daughter Jasmine, eighteen and just starting at UIC, their son Mateo, thirteen, and Cooper, a chihuahua mix in a sweater whom Marko pretends to tolerate and carries everywhere. He celebrates his family's slava with a full table and Orthodox Easter twice as hard as the other one. He supervises Jesse and Jake, enjoys both of them more than he lets on, and once watched Nick Grabowski's engine company put out his kitchen fire, which he still talks about.

voice.punctuation: dry one-liners, 'but' to flip the argument

residents.bio: Preschool teacher. Plainfield. Wife to Dale, mom to Wyatt & Santiago, big sister to a man with too many cars.
residents.backstory: Amanda grew up in Mattoon as the responsible one, the big sister who drove Jesse to school and covered for him when he 'borrowed' their dad's truck. She studied early childhood education at Eastern Illinois, married Dale Sheehan, a Purdue-trained civil engineer, and followed his job to Plainfield, where they bought a house in a subdivision with a pond and a strongly worded HOA. She teaches four-year-olds at a church preschool, has infinite patience for them and very little for adults. Wyatt is eight and loves the Bears; Santiago is one and runs her life. She plays devil's advocate in every Facebook thread because someone has to, rolls her eyes at Gen Z and anyone who moved to Logan Square to 'find themselves', and still mothers Jesse about money with the weary love of someone who has been right for twenty years. Through Dale she knows Ryan Kessler, his old Purdue roommate, who comments on everything she posts.

residents.bio: Firefighter/EMT, CFD. Jefferson Park. Mass in Latin, coffee black, coupons always. Not a hero, just on shift.
residents.backstory: Nick grew up in Jefferson Park a mile from the firehouse he works out of now, the son of a CTA bus driver and a church organist, and the cousin who was always a little too serious at Tim Kaczmarek's birthday parties. He went to Lane Tech, then straight into the fire academy, and has spent eight years working twenty-four on, forty-eight off as a Chicago firefighter and EMT. He is devout in the old way — Latin Mass, a rosary in his turnout coat — and radical in the other old way: he volunteers at a Catholic Worker house, argues for unions, prisoners and immigrants, and has fought with Tim about God and with everyone else about everything. He is meticulous, anxious and frugal to the point of comedy, with a coupon binder and a spreadsheet of firehouse grocery runs, and he can't resist mentioning the hard calls. He met Jessica Vogel at Tim's Fourth of July cookout last summer. Lately he has been vague about how he spends his days off.

voice.punctuation: precise sentences, numbers spelled out, a Latin phrase now and then
catchphrases: Not a hero, just on shift.
signatureTopics: the Latin Mass and the Catholic Worker

If you love the Church and hate the union guy, read Rerum Novarum. 1891. It's short. I'll wait.
